clue.text: Black day after detective's put out of action

blocks.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
sable is black in heraldry
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: A detective has a terrible day that leaves him out of action.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is': black and day come after the detective, giving DI + SABLE + D = DISABLED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disabled has been rendered inoperative, the same as being put out of action.

clue.text: Name encapsulates a new European river

indicators.note: to encapsulate is to enclose in a capsule, so one word holds the next ones

blocks.note: to dub is to give a name to
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A name contains a new European term.
explanation.walkthrough: D(AN)UB, then E.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danube is a major river of central Europe.

clue.text: Is upset by good quality autograph

indicators.note: upset means turned over, and in a down clue that flips the word bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
G is the abbreviation for good
a thing's nature is its essential quality

explanation.surface: A fan is disappointed by a well-made signed photo.
explanation.walkthrough: IS reversed gives SI, then G and NATURE.
explanation.definitionFit: An autograph is a person's handwritten name, a synonym for their signature.

clue.text: Where you may find an Araucaria declaration bang out of order

definitions.text: Where you may find an Araucaria

indicators.note: something out of order is not in its proper sequence, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, all fifteen letters

explanation.surface: Araucaria, the famous Guardian setter, makes a loud statement that breaks the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: Araucaria was a celebrated crossword setter's pseudonym, but it is also the monkey puzzle tree genus.
explanation.definitionFit: Araucaria is a genus of conifer, including the monkey puzzle tree, so a specimen would be planted in a public garden of plants.

clue.text: Upgrade rear of battle tank in shelter

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept
in places one word inside the following one

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
the lee is the sheltered side
a vat is a large tank for liquids

explanation.surface: An army improves the back of a tank sitting in cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tank' suggests the armoured vehicle of the battle, but it is a container for liquid; the lee is the side sheltered from the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: To elevate someone is to raise them in rank, the same as upgrading them.

clue.text: See farming implement picked up, one that's cold and tapered

indicators.note: picking up a signal means hearing it, so the words are taken by their sound

blocks.note: to eye is to see, and a sickle is a curved farming blade

explanation.surface: Someone spots a tool lying in a frosty field.
explanation.definitionFit: An icicle is a hanging spike of ice: cold, and narrowing to a point.

clue.text: Very nearly locating obscure rocks

indicators.note: rocks, as a verb, means shakes about, so these letters are jolted into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, all fifteen letters

explanation.surface: A geologist almost finds some hidden stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocks' looks like a noun for stones but works as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a near miss, an attempt that came very nearly to success.

clue.text: Cleaner welcomes current president

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one word holds another

blocks.note: a char, or charlady, is a British word for a cleaning woman
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady greets the country's sitting president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' reads as 'present-day' but is the physics symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A chair is the person presiding over a meeting, so the noun is a synonym for president.

clue.text: After start of equinox, definitely took ecstasy to provide protection against the sun

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
an emphatic agreement
had means took
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A spring raver takes ecstasy and then needs shade from the sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' merely sets the order: the E from equinox comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyeshade is a visor worn on the forehead to shield the eyes from sunlight.

clue.text: The job of a nurse is protecting everyone, first and foremost

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding it, so one word wraps around a letter
first and foremost points to the opening letter only

blocks.note: a carer looks after the sick, like a nurse
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A nurse's work is to protect everybody, above all else.
explanation.walkthrough: CARER goes around E.
explanation.definitionFit: A career is someone's profession or occupation, a synonym for their job.

clue.text: When do the lights go on? It's almost time

definitions.text: When do the lights go on?

blocks.note: nigh means nearly
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A question about when the lights come on, answered with 'nearly time'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' joins the question-definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamps are switched on after dark, so the period of darkness is when they go on.

clue.text: Fancy booze knocked back with salt

indicators.note: a drink knocked back is thrown backwards, so the word is read from end to start

blocks.note: ale is beer
a borate is a salt of boric acid

explanation.surface: Someone downs a drink with salt, as with tequila.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' looks like drinking the booze, but it turns the word round; borate is a chemistry term for a salt of boric acid.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaborate, as an adjective, means intricate or ornate, which is what fancy means.

clue.text: Webinar broadcast inspires a very brilliant idea

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, as seed is sown, so these letters are strewn into a new order
to inspire is to breathe in, so the result takes the next words inside it

blocks.note: the letters of the online seminar rearranged
taken as written
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: An online seminar sparks a clever thought in someone watching.
explanation.walkthrough: AV goes inside the reshuffled WEBINAR, between W and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainwave is a sudden clever inspiration, a synonym for a brilliant idea.

clue.text: What covers painting? Dirt

indicators.note: covering something means wrapping around it, so one word goes around the other

blocks.note: 'eh?' is a way of saying 'what?'
painting is a form of art

explanation.surface: A question about what lies on top of a painting, answered: dirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth in the sense of soil is a synonym for dirt.

clue.text: He's after unfinished fast food

indicators.note: something unfinished is missing its end, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: fast means quick
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man grabs a half-eaten takeaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast food' reads as one phrase, but 'fast' belongs to the wordplay and 'food' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiche is a savoury egg tart, an example of food.

clue.text: Made circumnavigation complete

blocks.note: first meaning: went all the way around, as a ship rounds a cape
second meaning: whole and well balanced

explanation.surface: A sailor finished a voyage around the world.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the past tense of going around something and an adjective for something whole or fully developed.

clue.text: Garment waste a wise man rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word is read in reverse

blocks.note: dung is animal waste
taken as written
a seer is a prophet or sage

explanation.surface: A sage throws away a ruined item of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: SEER reversed gives REES.
explanation.definitionFit: Dungarees are bib overalls, a garment of work trousers with a front panel.

clue.text: The Scots wander about with peculiar gravitas

indicators.note: peculiar means odd or strange, so these letters are set in an odd order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Scottish people stroll around with an odd seriousness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Scots' says the definition is a Scottish word, not a reference to people.
explanation.definitionFit: Stravaig is a Scots dialect verb meaning to roam or ramble aimlessly.

clue.text: Stiff drinks — they're often sought by darts players

definitions.text: they're often sought by darts players

blocks.note: first meaning: triple measures of spirits

blocks.clueFragment: they're often sought by darts players
blocks.note: second meaning: the narrow ring on a dartboard scoring three times the number

explanation.surface: A pub scene: strong drinks ordered by the darts team.
explanation.definitionFit: A triple measure of spirits and a dartboard's triple-scoring ring share one name.

clue.text: Confess about papers being biased

indicators.note: about means around, so one word surrounds the other

blocks.note: to sing is slang for confessing to the police
identity papers

explanation.surface: Someone owning up about newspapers that are partial.
explanation.definitionFit: Siding with one party means favouring it, which is being partial or biased.

clue.text: Type of table Director General takes home twice

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it within, so the outer letters wrap the rest

blocks.note: DG is the abbreviation for Director General
IN means at home, and twice doubles it

explanation.surface: A boss brings a piece of furniture home on two occasions.
explanation.definitionFit: A dining table is the kind used for meals, so the answer names a type of table.

clue.text: Ref endlessly took risks over winning goal

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the last letter drops
over means turned over, so in a down clue the letters are read upward

blocks.note: taken as written
diced, as in diced with death

explanation.surface: A referee gambled over a match-winning goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ref' loses its F to give RE; RE + DICED is then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A decider is the score that settles a match, such as a winning goal.

clue.text: Free end of string instrument lifted

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, so only that is kept
lifted means raised, so in a down clue the letters run upward

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
a sitar is an Indian stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A spare piece of instrument string gets stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifted' reads as stolen, but in a down clue it means the word is read from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratis means without charge, a synonym for free.

clue.text: A mountain? Don't be ridiculous!

blocks.note: an alp is a high mountain
a scornful exclamation

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at a hill being called a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' looks like the article but is the definition: alpha is the Greek letter A.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the first letter of the Greek alphabet, the counterpart of A, and is A in the radio alphabet.

clue.text: Ring encircling middle of spherical gem

indicators.note: encircling means surrounding, so one word goes around a letter
the middle of a word is its central letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: a peal is a ring of bells
the fifth of nine letters

explanation.surface: A ring set around a round jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' suggests jewellery but is a peal of bells.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearl is a lustrous gem formed inside an oyster.

clue.text: One may be placed on a beach to monitor risk, according to Spooner

definitions.text: One may be placed on a beach

indicators.note: Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words, so the starts are exchanged

blocks.note: to monitor is to check, and a risk is a dare

explanation.surface: Something is positioned on the sand to keep watch for danger, like a lifeguard's post.
explanation.definitionFit: A deckchair is a folding canvas seat often set out on beaches.

clue.text: Left rehab, and one deteriorated, to some extent

indicators.note: only to some extent means only a part of the following words is used

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word into the next three

explanation.surface: Someone checked out of rehab and their condition got worse.
explanation.definitionFit: Left, as a past participle, means deserted or forsaken.

clue.text: Enormous jar, so it's said

indicators.note: something said is spoken, so we listen for the sound of the word

blocks.note: to grate on someone is to jar

explanation.surface: A description of a huge pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jar' looks like a container, but it is the verb meaning to irritate.
explanation.definitionFit: Great in its basic sense means very large, a synonym for enormous.

clue.text: Lead source of wind starts to nip away

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only those are kept

blocks.note: a gale is a strong wind
the opening letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A cold wind's first nip goes away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' is the metal, not leading.
explanation.definitionFit: Galena is lead sulphide, the main ore from which lead is extracted.

clue.text: Starmer's struggling to produce bits of 7

indicators.note: a struggling person is in disarray, so these letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: the Labour leader's name with its possessive S

explanation.surface: Keir Starmer, the UK Labour leader, is under pressure from a 'chair' (cross-reference to 7).
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 7 is CHAIR; armrests are parts of a chair.
explanation.definitionFit: Armrests are the side supports of a chair, so they are parts of one.
